text: I'll start by checking the environment and sketching the blade camber math before building anything.
Blade camber: θ(r) linear in r with total wrap 30° backward. I'll build the 2D blade section in mm and check the measured wrap angle and thickness before extruding.
Now the fluid volume: annulus (hub r=12 to r=58, z 0→14) minus the 7 blades, no fillets yet. Coarse look first.
Now attempt the 2 mm root fillets on the fluid's blade/backplate edges — the request asks me to try and report if they can't survive.

The 2 mm fillet is geometrically impossible here (2+2 mm > the 3 mm blade thickness at the blunt ends) and is far below the cell size — I'll drop it and say so. Now rebuild the fluid split at r=16 so the inlet and shroud are separate faces.
The fuse merged the coplanar top faces, so I'll split the top face by boolean with a r=16 disc instead, classify all faces, and export per-patch STLs in **metres**.
Faces are faceted (1092 blade faces from the polyline). Rebuilding the blade sides as splines gives clean surfaces and sane feature edges; then re-classify.
Exporting the six patch STLs in metres, then checking the welded union's free edges myself before meshing.
1660 free edges — but my weld tolerance (1e-9 m) is tighter than float32 STL precision. Re-weld at 1e-7 m.
Meshing first. Coarse background block (~2 mm cells) around the passage, then snappy with the six surfaces.
Mesh exists. Now look at it and check patch areas against the geometry.

The picture is right. Now fix the STL union: per-face exports gave 1660 free edges because each face was tessellated independently. I'll split the solid at r=16 topologically, mesh the whole shape once, and write the STLs from the shared triangulation.
Re-emitting the split self-contained so it lives in the script.
Now classify faces per solid (so orientation stays outward), drop the internal r=16 seam faces, and write STLs from one shared triangulation.
Watertight and consistently wound. Check normals point out of the fluid, then refine: feature edges plus level 2 on the blades.
Final render of the refined mesh, plus the numbers I'll report.

Mesh is built and `checkMesh` is clean.

**What I built** — the wetted passage of the impeller, in metres: the annulus from the hub surface (r = 12 mm) to the outlet (r = 58 mm), between backplate top (z = 0) and shroud (z = 14 mm), with 7 backward-curved blades cut out.

**Measured against the request:** blade wrap LE→TE = 30.000° backward (θ linear in r); LE r = 16.000 mm, TE cut at r = 58.000 mm (mesh bbox 0.05800 m); blade thickness 3 mm normal to camber (section area 143.55 mm² vs 143.55 mm² for a 3 mm-wide swept band); 7 blades (7 separate outlet arc segments); blade/shroud height 14 mm (mesh z-max 0.01404 m); hub patch area 1.056e-3 m² = 2π·0.012·0.014 exactly; inlet annulus 3.50e-4 m² (full 12→16 mm annulus is 3.52e-4; the blunt leading edges poke 0.07 mm inside r = 16). Mesh volume 1.2801e-4 m³ vs CAD 1.2792e-4 m³ (+0.07 %, snapping). 174 529 cells, max non-orth 54.4, max skewness 2.04, one region.

**Fillets removed, as allowed.** The 2 mm blade-root fillet is not constructible here: two 2 mm fillets on opposite sides of a 3 mm-thick blade overlap at the blunt ends, and OCC refused the radius. It is also ~1.5× the 1 mm surface cell and would not survive snapping. The blade/hub fillet has no referent at all — the leading edge is at r = 16 mm and the hub is at r = 12 mm, so blades never touch the hub.

**My choices, not given:** inlet is the annular opening 12 < r < 16 mm at z = 14 mm (the shroud covers r = 16→58 mm, so this is where axial flow enters past the hub); blade camber θ linear in r; blunt LE/TE; background cell 2 mm, level 1 on all walls, level 2 on blades, no boundary layers. **Not modelled, because they are not wetted by this passage:** backplate 60 mm radius and 4 mm thickness, and hub height 18 mm — the fluid sees only the backplate top face out to r = 58 and the hub cylinder up to z = 14.
